# CosmoIknosLab/PathJev
**Stars**: 1 | **Language**: Python
**Description**: This repository hosts the code for PathJev, a decision-native vision-language model specifically designed for histopathology. It includes functionalities for data preparation (training and testing), model training (PathJev-P and a generative baseline), evaluation metrics, a whole-slide cluster-labeling pipeline, and code to reproduce all figures and tables from the associated paper. The model itself is based on MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head, capable of outputting probability distributions over runtime-chosen candidate answers in a single forward pass. It supports multiple question types: one-of-K choices, yes/no, and ordered levels.

## src/pathjev/evaluate.py ``` """Score a model's decision distributions against PathJev states. python -m pathjev.evaluate --states _patch.jsonl [...] --decisions /_decisions.jsonl \ --out /eval.json `--decisions` is the output of upstream `scripts/infer_medjev.py` (one row per state: {"state_id", "distributions": {qid: {candidate_id: prob}}}) or any baseline written in the same format. For every (dataset, qid) the evaluator reports: choice / noul: metrics.summary (accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro-F1, ECE, adaptive ECE, Brier, NLL, AURC) on one-hot targets, plus a group-bootstrap CI for ECE and balanced accuracy; score: expected-level MAE and ranked probability score (RPS). Soft-target decisions (mixed mosaics) are scored for the homogeneity Noul only; their composition targets are reported as total-variation distance. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import json from collections import defaultdict from pathlib import Path import numpy as np from pathjev import metrics, stats from pathjev.groups import state_group def _read(paths): for path in paths: for line in Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8"): if line.strip(): yield json.loads(line) def collect(state_paths, decision_paths) -> dict[tuple[str, str], dict]: """Group aligned (probs, target, group) per (dataset, qid).""" preds = {row["state_id"]: row["distributions"] for row in _read(decision_paths)} table: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = defaultdict(lambda: {"probs": [], "target": [], "groups": [], "type": None, "kinds": set(), "ids": None, "missing": 0}) for state in _read(state_paths): dist = preds.get(state["state_id"]) meta = state.get("meta", {}) for d in state["decisions"]: key = (meta.get("dataset", "?"), d["qid"]) entry = table[key] ids = [c["id"] for c in d["candidates"]] if dist is None or d["qid"] not in dist: entry["missing"] += 1 continue entry["type"] = d["type"] entry["kinds"].add(d.get("target_kind", "one_hot")) entry["ids"] = entry["ids"] or ids if ids != entry["ids"]: raise ValueError(f"{key}: candidate order differs between states; align before scoring") p = np.array([dist[d["qid"]].get(i, 0.0) for i in ids], dtype=float) entry["probs"].append(p / p.sum() if p.sum() > 0 else p) entry["target"].append(np.array([d["target"][i] for i in ids], dtype=float)) entry["groups"].append(state_group(state)) return table def score_entry(entry: dict, resamples: int) -> dict: probs, target = np.stack(entry["probs"]), np.stack(entry["target"]) groups = np.array(entry["groups"]) out = {"type": entry["type"], "n": int(len(probs)), "missing": entry["missing"], "n_groups": int(len(set(entry["groups"]))), "candidates": entry["ids"]} soft = ~np.isclose(target.max(axis=1), 1.0) if soft.any(): out["n_soft"] = int(soft.sum()) out["soft_total_variation"] = float(0.5 * np.abs(probs[soft] - target[soft]).sum(axis=1).mean()) hard = ~soft if not hard.any(): return out p, y, g = probs[hard], target[hard].argmax(axis=1), groups[hard] if entry["type"] == "score": levels = np.arange(p.shape[1]) expected = (p * levels).sum(axis=1) cdf_p, cdf_t = np.cumsum(p, axis=1), np.cumsum(np.eye(p.shape[1])[y], axis=1) out.update({"mae_expected_level": float(np.abs(expected - y).mean()), "rps": float(((cdf_p - cdf_t) ** 2).sum(axis=1).mean() / (p.shape[1] - 1)), **{f"choice_{k}": v for k, v in metrics.summary(p, y).items()}}) return out out.update(metrics.summary(p, y)) if resamples: out["ece_ci95"] = list(stats.bootstrap_ci(lambda idx: metrics.ece(p[idx], y[idx]), len(y), g, resamples=resamples)[1:]) out["balanced_accuracy_ci95"] = list(stats.bootstrap_ci( lambda idx: metrics.balanced_accuracy(y[idx], p[idx].argmax(axis=1)), len(y), g, resamples=resamples)[1:]) out["reliability"] = metrics.reliability_curve(p, y) return out def main() -> None: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter) ap.add_argument("--states", nargs="+", required=True) ap.add_argument("--decisions", nargs="+", required=True) ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path) ap.add_argument("--resamples", type=int, default=2000) args = ap.parse_args() table = collect(args.states, args.decisions) report = {f"{dataset}/{qid}": score_entry(entry, args.resamples) for (dataset, qid), entry in sorted(table.items()) if entry["probs"]} args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) args.out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=1)) for key, row in report.items(): print(key, {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in row.items() if isinstance(v, float)}) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ## README.md ``` # PathJev: decision-native vision–language modelling for histopathology [![Model on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Model-Cristiandieti%2FPathJev--P-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/Cristiandieti/PathJev-P) [![Demo on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Demo-PathJev--P--demo-orange)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Cristiandieti/PathJev-P-demo) [![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/CosmoIknosLab/PathJev/blob/main/inference/PathJev_demo.ipynb) [![Code licence: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-Apache--2.0-blue)](LICENSE) PathJev is a decision-native vision–language model for histopathology. Given an image, a question and a set of candidate answers chosen at run time, it returns a normalised probability distribution over the candidates, including "none of these", in a single forward pass. It handles three question types: one of K classes (Choice), yes or no (Noul) and ordered levels (Score). The model is MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head that reads the hidden states at marker tokens closing each candidate. Training data are built deterministically from expert pathology annotations, with organ-specific candidate sets and whole organs held out for testing.

This repository contains the code to build the training and test data, train PathJev-P and the generative baseline, evaluate all methods, run the whole-slide cluster-labelling pipeline, and regenerate every table, figure and number of the paper. - **Paper:** Cristian Tommasino and Antonio M. Rinaldi, *PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology*, preprint, 2026 (arXiv link to be added). - **Code:** https://github.com/CosmoIknosLab/PathJev (this repository). - **Model weights:** https://huggingface.co/Cristiandieti/PathJev-P (non-commercial research use; MedGemma HAI-DEF terms). - **Demo:** https://huggingface.co/spaces/Cristiandieti/PathJev-P-demo (precomputed examples). The model repository also has a Colab notebook for live use on a free GPU. Not intended or validated for clinical use. ## Quick start: use the trained model The trained PathJev-P weights (LoRA adapter and decision head) are on Hugging Face, at [Cristiandieti/PathJev-P](https://huggingface.co/Cristiandieti/PathJev-P). You need access to the base model `google/medgemma-1.5-4b-it`: accept its terms on Hugging Face and log in with `huggingface-cli login`. To try it without installing anything, open the [Colab notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/github/CosmoIknosLab/PathJev/blob/main/inference/PathJev_demo.ipynb), which runs on a free GPU. ```python # pip install "transformers>=4.50" peft bitsandbytes accelerate pillow huggingface_hub (4-bit needs a CUDA GPU) import sys from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download local = snapshot_download("Cristiandieti/PathJev-P") # weights + inference code sys.path.insert(0, local) from pathjev_infer import PathJev model = PathJev.load(local, token=True) probs = model.predict("patch.png", [{ "instructions": "Which Gleason pattern predominates in this prostate tissue?", "candidates": [{"id": "benign", "text": "benign (non-cancerous) prostate tissue"}, {"id": "gp3", "text": "Gleason pattern 3 carcinoma"}, {"id": "gp4", "text": "Gleason pattern 4 carcinoma"}, {"id": "gp5", "text": "Gleason pattern 5 carcinoma"}]}], add_other=True) print(probs[0]) # one probability per candidate, plus "other" ``` The same inference code is in [`inference/pathjev_infer/`](inference/pathjev_infer/). The weights are for non-commercial research use under the MedGemma (HAI-DEF) terms, and they are not intended for clinical use. ## Whole-slide use PathJev can name tissue clusters in a whole slide. Tiles are embedded with H-optimus-0 and grouped by a Gaussian mixture with soft memberships; PathJev-P is run on the most typical tiles of each cluster, abstains when unsure, and cluster probabilities are propagated back to every tile.

The example below is a gastric slide from HiESD, an organ never seen in training. It shows, from top left: the thumbnail, the region annotation, the clusters, the cluster labels (grey: abstain), PathJev-P on every tile, and the adenocarcinoma probability propagated from the clusters. This is a qualitative demonstration on four slides. The fine-grained gastric classes are mostly not recognised, while the coarse question "is adenocarcinoma present?" is answered well (see the paper).
